prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. The attached image is a STYLE REFERENCE for an original chibi football player asset pack, not a sheet to preserve literally. Match the lovely compact two-head-tall proportions, thick crisp dark outlines, big readable eyes, tiny sturdy legs and restrained retro pixel shading of its characters. Create a PRODUCTION SOURCE sprite sheet with NINE versions of ONE IDENTICAL adult male chibi footballer, arranged precisely in 3 columns and 3 rows with equal cell sizes. ALL nine have IDENTICAL neutral standing pose, arms slightly away from sides, both feet on same baseline, facing front with a slight three-quarter face toward viewer-right. Same face, same light warm peach skin, same turquoise plain football shirt, turquoise shorts, turquoise socks with white cuffs, charcoal boots. NO ball, gloves, beard, jewellery, captain band, lettering or logos. Only HAIR SHAPE changes per cell, reading left to right top to bottom: short tidy crop; side swept long fringe; shoulder length hair with plain white thin headband; compact mohawk; slicked-back hair; very short buzz cut; round tight curly afro; top knot bun; spiky hair. All hair dark charcoal with subtle slate highlights. Absolute consistency in body, face placement and scale across all nine, leave generous transparent padding per cell. Full bodies fully inside their cells, no overlaps, no text or labels. Hard square pixel clusters and intentional pixel steps, no smoothing, no gradients, no painted shading. Each sprite should resemble an actual 48x64 pixel game character enlarged with nearest-neighbor, rich enough to retain the selected style without becoming high resolution illustration. IMPORTANT transparent alpha background throughout, absolutely no black fill, checkerboard, scenery, ground plane or cast shadow. Do not redraw nine different character identities: same canonical face and body, nine hairstyles only.
processing: nearest-neighbor normalization, binary alpha, indexed materials; no gameplay/save data changes
